chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
No one is to be imprisoned for ever except for three: One who severely tortures someone, and the woman who reneges from Al-Islam, and the thief (who steals) after the cutting of the hand and the leg.

key_terms.قَطْعِ الْيَدِ وَالرِّجْلِ: Cutting of the hand and the leg (amputation)
key_terms.يُخَلَّدُ: To be imprisoned for ever / permanent imprisonment
key_terms.يُمَثِّلُ: To severely torture / practice tamthil (inflicting severe pain or mutilation)

ai.seo_question: Who are the three people subject to permanent imprisonment in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi specifies three categories subject to permanent imprisonment (khulud): those who inflict severe torture (tamthil), apostate women, and recidivist thieves after amputation. This ruling highlights the distinct treatment of female apostates compared to males and underscores the severity of persistent theft despite corporal punishment, reflecting the principle of preventing further harm through indefinite detention.
